chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام; and from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, who said:
I presented the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and he said: “It is authentic.

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning the blood-money for injuries to all the limbs—in the head, the face, and the rest of the body; hearing, sight, voice, intellect, the two hands, and the two legs—in cases of severing, fracture, cracking, crushing, exposing the bone, bleeding wounds, displacement of bones, and penetrating wounds, whenever any of that occurs. So whatever bone is broken and then heals without deformity or defect, and no bone is displaced from it, then its blood-money is known. If it exposes the bone and no bones are displaced from it, then its fracture and the blood-money of its exposing wound are established; and the blood-money of every bone that is broken is known, and the displacement of its bones is half the blood-money of its fracture, and the blood-money of its exposing wound is one quarter of the blood-money of its fracture, in those parts covered by clothing, excluding the two bones of the forearm and the fingers.

And regarding the blood-money of the amputated part, it is one third of the blood-money of that bone in which it is found. And he gave the legal ruling concerning a penetrating wound, when it penetrates from a spear or a dagger into some part of a man’s limbs, that its blood-money is one tenth of the blood-money of the man: one hundred dinars.”

key_terms.النَّافِذَةِ: a wound that passes through or penetrates
key_terms.الْكَسْرِ: fracture or breaking of a bone
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: an injury that exposes the bone
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a dinar, used here as the unit for compensation
key_terms.دِيَةِ: blood-money or legal financial compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.نَقْلِ الْعِظَامِ: displacement or shifting of bones from their place

ai.seo_question: What does the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام state about diyah for fractures and bodily injuries?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the authenticity of the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام and records legal rulings of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding blood-money for bodily injuries. It details compensations for fractures, exposed bones, displaced bones, amputations, and penetrating wounds across various parts of the body.
